Insulin degludec ( Tresiba )
AWMSG Advice No 2816 recommends insulin degludec (Tresiba) as an option for the treatment of diabetes mellitus in adult patients where treatment with a basal insulin analogue is considered appropriate.
Insulin degludec (Tresiba) is not recommended for the treatment of diabetes mellitus in adolescents and children from the age of 1 year.
Note Tresiba is available in FlexTouch pens as both 100units/ml and 200units/ml - the strength must be specified when prescribing and in patient records.
AWMSG 5196 : Insulin degludec (Tresiba ® ) is recommended as an option for use within NHS Wales for the treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children from the age of 1 year (added 7/11/22)
• Tresiba FlexTouch 100units/ml solution for injection 3ml pre-filled pen
• Tresiba FlexTouch 200units/ml solution for injection 3ml pre-filled pen
• Tresiba Penfill 100units/ml solution for injection 3ml cartridges
Prescribing Notes

https://www.nice.org.uk/advice/ktt20/chapter/evidence-context#insulin-prescribing-and-administration-reducing-errors

Insulin degludec + Liraglutide
06.01.02.03 (Other antidiabetic drugs) > [Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) Agonists]
Date added to formulary : 23-01-2020
Formulary Status:
A     -  Amber
Medicines Available :
Insulin degludec + Liraglutide ( Xultophy )
AWMSG Advice No 2715 recommends Xultophy as an option for use in combination with oral glucose-lowering medicinal products when these combined with basal insulin do not provide adequate glycaemic control.
Note:
i. This advice covers a narrower population than the licensed indication. This reflects Novo Nordisk’s submission which focussed the use of Xultophy as an add-on therapy for patients whose glucose levels were uncontrolled on basal insulin
ii. AWMSG’s FAR additionally advised that Xultophy should be prescribed by brand name to avoid medication errors.
In adults with type 2 diabetes NICE NG28 recommends:
• Only offer a GLP-1 mimetic in combination with insulin with specialist care advice and ongoing support from a consultant-led multidisciplinary team. A consultant-led multidisciplinary team may include a wide range of staff based in primary, secondary and community care.
• Only continue GLP-1 mimetic therapy if the person with type 2 diabetes has had a beneficial metabolic response (a reduction of at least 11 mmol/mol [1.0%] in HbA1c and a weight loss of at least 3% of initial body weight in 6 months).
• Xultophy 100units/ml / 3.6mg/ml solution for injection 3ml pre-filled pen

Insulin glargine
06.01.01.02 (Intermediate- and long-acting insulins)
Date added to formulary : no date recorded
Formulary Status:
A     -  Amber
Medicines Available :
Insulin glargine 300units/mL ( Toujeo )
1. Use of  Toujeo may be considered only where patients are experiencing significant problems due to the volume of the insulin being injected (due to the high dose of the 100units/mL insulin). This may include patients having to use divided doses of long-acting insulin analogues but who require administration by a third party such as a District Nurse.
2.  Toujeo should only be initiated by specialists in diabetes (this includes accredited GPs with a specialist interest in diabetes and DSN non medical prescribers).
3. Prescribers should always include the strength in units/mL on the prescription when prescribing any pen device of insulin glargine – CHMP’s educational guide advises the brand Toujeo should be written.
4. Patients transferred should be instructed to closely monitor their glucose levels during the transfer and in the following weeks. Toujeo is not bioequivalent to insulin glargine 100units/ml ( Lantus ) and dose adjustment is needed.
5. Letters informing GP practices that a patient has been transferred onto a high dose insulin should indicate this clearly (through use of bold type) early on in the text.
MHRA advice on high strength insulins  (April 2015).
• Toujeo 300units/mL solution for injection 1.5mL pre-filled disposable devices
• Toujeo 300units/ml solution for injection 3ml pre-filled DoubleStar pen
Prescribing Notes
All healthcare professionals should refer to NICE advice - Safer insulin prescribing:
https://www.nice.org.uk/advice/ktt20/chapter/evidence-context#insulin-prescribing-and-administration-reducing-errors

Type 1 diabetes mellitus. Should only be considered for type 2 diabetes mellitus if:
the patient requires assistance from a carer or healthcare professional to administer their insulin injection
the patient's lifestyle is significantly restricted by recurrent symptomatic hypoglycaemic episodes or
they would otherwise need twice daily basal insulin injections in combination with oral antidiabetic drugs
AWMSG 0413 - Lantus
Treatment of type 1 diabetes mellitus in children aged 2 to less than 6 years.
Abasaglar®
AWMSG 3215 - Abasaglar
Treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents, and children aged 2 years and above.
Abasaglar is a biosimilar and is approved within its licensed indication in accordance with NICE or AWMSG guidance for insulin glargine (Lantus), the reference product.
It is not recommended for use within NHS Wales outside of these circumstances.
Toujeo®
"Toujeo" - insulin glargine 300IU/mL in a pre-filled pen is recommended for the treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults and children aged 6-18 years ONLY within the following patient groups;
Where the flexibility of injection timings (+/- 3 hours) due to proven poor glycaemic control attributable to problems with timing of daily insulin would be beneficial
Repeated and unpleasant hypoglycaemic episodes that significantly affect their way of life
Experiencing pain on injection,   or having to split long-acting insulin doses for comfort
On split doses of long acting analogue insulin administered by a healthcare professional, where the second visit from the helathcare professional is for the sole purpose of delivering the second dose of insulin.
NOTE: Prescribe by brand
